name: The Necromancer Animation kit raises a Ghoul, applies Fetid Ward to it and the pet deals damage
contract: The 'necro' actor is solo with a kit (Task 3/4 mechanism) whose opener casts Fetid Ward (680388, CharacterAdvancement 29244) before Raise: Ghoul (500971, CharacterAdvancement 33775) so a new Ghoul (creature 50073) inherits the ward at creation (AscensionNecromancerSummons.cpp: a new minion copies any of 680388/681460/681529 active on the owner). Fetid Ward's own aura id, checked everywhere in AscensionNecromancerEvents.cpp/AscensionNecromancerAuras.cpp, is 680388 itself (680388's own apply-aura effect on TARGET_UNIT_CASTER), not the spell (681463) it periodically triggers. The upkeep rules resummon the Ghoul when owned_below 1 and refresh Fetid Ward (recast 680388 on self) when pet_aura_missing on 680388. The opener sequence is also run explicitly as plain 'cast' steps right after the talent purchase, before any stage, so the Ghoul-carries-Fetid-Ward assertion is checked on a living Ghoul: the stage's own internal opener (Task 4) would only run again if the Ghoul were missing, and a loss against a real elite can kill the Ghoul before the assertion runs. balance_stage against one level 36 Scarlet Soldier (4286, the Task 2/4/5 dungeon spawn) separately proves pets_owned_start and damage_done_pets are non-zero (the pets_missing rule in Task 8 flags a kit whose pets never spawn or never deal damage); that stage's own opener is a no-op here because the Ghoul already exists, so pets_owned_start reflects the same pre-raised Ghoul.
